title: Study of Cerebral Activation During Different Rehabilitation Tasks in Mirror Therapy in Healthy Subjects
brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to investigate the cerebral activation during Classic Mirror Therapy (TMC) and especially during Virtual Mirror Therapy (TMV) in healthy subjects. It seems that the precuneus is involved in the effectiveness of mirror therapy. One goal of this study is to determine if there is a better activation of the precuneus during TMV than during TMC. Others goals are to compare cerebral activation during three different tasks (TMV, TMC and a simple motor task), to study the intra-subjects reproducibility of the measurement and the correlation between cerebral activation and feelings of the participants about the efficacity of the tasks.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age:18 to 40
* Right handed
* No neurological disease

Exclusion Criteria:

* Known allergy to components of the fNIRS device: neoprene
